All right, the user’s last request was to “use deepseek v4 flash on max reasoning.” I’ve already updated the repository to use the DeepSeek‑v4‑flash model by setting `OPENCODE_MODEL = "opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free"` in `ralph.py` and by creating an `opencode.json` that configures that model with `"reasoningEffort": "high"`. I also added a couple of test files (`test_ralph_helpers.py`) that import the new `ralph` module and verify its helper functions.

Now that the new `ralph.py` module lives at the repository root (i.e., alongside the `Makefile`), the existing lint and fix targets in the `Makefile` will not run any static analysis on it. The current `Makefile` looks like this:

```
lint:
	$(VENV)/bin/ruff format --check src/ tests/
	$(VENV)/bin/ruff check src/ tests/
	$(PY) -m mypy --strict src/ tests/

fix:
	$(VENV)/bin/ruff format src/ tests/
	$(VENV)/bin/ruff check --fix src/ tests/
```

These commands only touch `src/` and `tests/`. Since `ralph.py` is a top‑level file, it will be ignored by both `ruff` and `mypy`, which means linting and type‑checking will miss potential issues in the newly added code. That could cause CI failures later, especially because the tests I just added import `ralph` and will be run under the same linting pipeline.

Therefore, I need to modify the `Makefile` so that the lint and fix commands also include `ralph.py`. The simplest way is to append `ralph.py` to each of the command lines that already list `src/ tests/`. I’ll keep the existing formatting and just add the file name after the other paths.

I’ll perform a targeted edit (not a global replace) because the block I’m changing appears exactly once. I’ll replace the old block with the new block that includes `ralph.py`. This will ensure that future `make lint` and `make fix` runs will check the new module, keeping the repository’s quality gates intact.
